subject: Lumina Health — entry gate sprint plan & API seeding convergence
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Sara Klein <sara.klein@luminahealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-30 15:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Lumina Health — entry gate sprint plan & API seeding convergence

Hi Sara — thanks again for the sync today. Per our conversation I wanted to put a short, runnable plan in this thread so we can drive the initial tenant activation this week. Goal: have Lumina's staging and prod tenants seeded with service accounts, API keys, and an initial admin roster by end of next week so your engineers can run integration tests.

Quick runbook (initial sprint):
- Deliverables (this week):
  - Seed two projects (staging / prod) and create 1 service-account per environment.
  - Generate short-lived service keys (exported into your secrets manager) and a single infra user API key for feature toggle tests.
  - Invite 4 admins into the prod workspace and 6 engineers into staging.
  - Complete KMS binding for encryption-at-rest (if you want Redwood-managed KMS we can handle the handshake; otherwise share your KMS ARN).
- Owner/next steps:
  - Action: Please confirm the list of admins & engineers we should invite (names + emails) — due EOD tomorrow. (onboard@luminahealth.com is CC'd)
  - Connor O'Brien (cc) will prepare the service-account template and a sample key rotation cadence.
  - Monica Patel (cc) will draft the invite cadence and role matrix to match your internal teams.
- Security note:
  - Recommended pattern: server-to-server integrations use service-account keys + rotation; developer access via SSO or short-lived user tokens. We will not seed long-lived personal API keys in prod.

Attachments: Lumina_Mutual_Action_Plan_v1.pdf (MAP), sample_project_role_matrix.csv

Links: onboarding doc (https://redwood.company/handbooks/onboard-tenant-sdk) and a scheduling link if you'd like to accelerate the handoff call: https://calendly.com/redwood/ev-handoff-30

Proposed quick milestone: schedule a 30-min activation call tomorrow morning to walk through the seed flow and share the seed artifacts. If that works, confirm preferred time and we’ll send invites.

Thanks — looking forward to kicking this off.

—
Evelyn Hart
Implementation Manager | Customer Success
Redwood Inference
From: Sara Klein <sara.klein@luminahealth.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-09-30 16:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Lumina Health — entry gate sprint plan & API seeding convergence

Hi Evelyn — thanks for the clear plan. A few clarifying questions before we lock times: 
1) API key scoping: can you confirm the recommended default scopes for service-account keys vs user keys? We want least-privilege by default.
2) SSO vs Redwood-managed invites: we are mid-Okta setup (team SSO scheduled next week). Can we be invited using Redwood-managed accounts now and transition to SSO later without re-provisioning work?
3) Env separation: how isolated are staging and prod projects? Will secrets from staging be prevented from being exported to prod by the default config?
4) KMS: we will need to know exactly which permissions the service account needs to bind to our KMS (we run AWS KMS).

We can do the activation call tomorrow morning at 10:00 PT. I’ll ask our infra lead (onboard@luminahealth.com) to share the admin list after this message.

Also please confirm whether the seed keys you generate are single-use exportable files or if you recommend seeding into our vault via an automated rotation flow.

—Sara
Sara Klein
Head of Integrations | Lumina Health

To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-30 17:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Lumina Health — entry gate sprint plan & API seeding convergence

Quick internal note — I’ll produce the service-account template and a seed script (bash + example where we push into Hashi Vault). Estimated first draft in 3 hours. —Connor
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Sara Klein <sara.klein@luminahealth.com>, Lumina Health Onboarding <onboard@luminahealth.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-30 17:25:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Lumina Health — entry gate sprint plan & API seeding convergence

Sara — great questions, answered inline below and in the attached updated MAP.

1) API key scoping
- Service-account keys: scoped to project-level runtime + ingest endpoints (minimal: tokens:write, models:invoke). We avoid admin scopes on service keys.
- User keys: short-lived (recommended TTL 8h) for developers; these have broader read-only debug scopes but not billing/admin.

2) SSO vs Redwood-managed invites
- You can absolutely onboard with Redwood-managed accounts now. We provide a migration path: when Okta is ready we perform a canonical account-linking step (map email -> SSO identity) so users keep their existing role assignments; no re-provisioning of project artifacts required. We’ll coordinate the mapping during the SSO cutover call.

3) Env separation
- Staging and prod are separate projects and isolated by default. Secrets cannot be exported across projects via Redwood tooling unless an operator performs an explicit copy. We will keep the seed scripts scoped to staging/prod separately.

4) KMS permissions
- Minimum IAM permissions (AWS): kms:CreateGrant, kms:Decrypt, kms:DescribeKey on the specific key resource. Connor will include an inline snippet in the seed repo.

Seed key format and delivery
- We recommend seeding directly into your vault via our rotation endpoint (automated flow). If you prefer an initial one-time export we can provide a single-use encrypted key bundle which you can import into your vault. For long-term we prefer the automated flow for auditability.

Call: we’ve scheduled a 30-min activation walkthrough for 2026-10-01 10:00 PT (Zoom) — invite sent separately. Meeting link: https://zoom.us/j/1234567890

I’ve attached an updated MAP reflecting the KMS snippet and a sample role matrix. Connor/Monica will drop the seed artifacts in the shared drive before the call.

Thanks — see you tomorrow.

—
Evelyn Hart
Implementation Manager | Customer Success
Redwood Inference
